'''Jarron Cumberland''' (born September 22, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Maccabi Ra'anana]] of the Israeli [[Liga Leumit (basketball)|Liga Leumit]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati Bearcats]].

==High school career==
Cumberland attended [[Wilmington High School (Ohio)|Wilmington High School]] in [[Wilmington, Ohio]]. He committed to playing college basketball for [[Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball|Cincinnati]] over offers from [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], [[Xavier Musketeers men's basketball|Xavier]] and others.<ref>{{cite web|first=Brendan F.|last=Quinn|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2015/07/2016_sg_jarron_cumberland_a_mi.html|title=2016 SG Jarron Cumberland, a Michigan recruit, commits to Cincinnati|work=[[MLive]]|date=July 15, 2015|access-date=March 13, 2019}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman, Cumberland came off the bench, averaging 19.1 minutes, 8.3 points and 2.4 rebounds per game, earning a place on the [[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) all-freshman team and he shared Sixth Man of the Year honors with Ben Emelogu of [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|SMU]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Brendan F.|last=Quinn|url=https://cincinnati.rivals.com/news/caupain-named-sportsman-of-the-year-and-cumberland-sixth-man-for-aac|title=Caupain named Sportsman of the year and Cumberland Sixth Man for AAC|work=[[Rivals.com]]|date=March 8, 2017|access-date=March 13, 2019}}</ref> As a sophomore, Cumberland moved into the starting lineup, averaging 11.5 points, 4 rebounds and 2.9 assists per game as the Bearcats went 31–5, earning a 2 seed in the [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018 NCAA tournament]]. The team's Final Four hopes were cut short with a second-round loss to [[Nevada Wolf Pack men's basketball|Nevada]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Tom|last=Groeschen|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2018/03/19/recapping-uc-bearcats-season-and-devastating-ncaa-loss-and-look-ahead/438588002/|title=Recapping UC Bearcats' season and devastating NCAA loss, and a look ahead|work=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]]|date=March 19, 2018|access-date=March 13, 2019}}</ref>

After losing stars [[Gary Clark (basketball)|Gary Clark]], [[Jacob Evans]] and Kyle Washington for the [[2018–19 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2018–19 season]], junior Cumberland moved into the primary scoring role for the Bearcats.<ref>{{cite web|first=Tristan|last=Freeman|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2018/07/18/cincinnati-basketball-rising-junior-jarron-cumberland-set-break-2018-19/|title=Cincinnati Basketball: Rising junior Jarron Cumberland to lead the Bearcats in 2018-19|work=[[FanSided]]|date=July 18, 2018|access-date=March 13, 2019}}</ref> Cumberland averaged 18.8 points, 4.4 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game. At the conclusion of the season, Cumberland was named AAC Player of the Year.<ref>{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Springer|url=https://www.cincinnati.com/story/sports/college/university-of-cincinnati/2019/03/13/cumberland-voted-aac-player-year-league-coaches/3151243002/|title=UC Bearcats guard Jarron Cumberland snares AAC Player of the Year honors|work=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]]|date=March 13, 2019|access-date=March 13, 2019}}</ref>

Cumberland suffered a foot injury in the preseason. Three games into his senior season, Cumberland was benched for one game by new coach [[John Brannen (basketball)|John Brannen]]. Cumberland's ill-advised halfcourt shot contributed to a one-point loss to [[Colgate Raiders men's basketball|Colgate]] on December 14, 2019. In January 2020, Cumberland scored 22 points in a win at [[Temple Owls men's basketball|Temple]], including 14 of the last 16 points.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Wallner |first1=Jeff |title=The old Jarron Cumberland is back, perhaps just in time to salvage the season for the UC Bearcats |url=https://www.wcpo.com/college-sports/university-of-cincinnati/the-old-jarron-cumberland-is-back-perhaps-just-in-time-to-salvage-the-season-for-the-uc-bearcats |access-date=March 11, 2020 |work=WCPO |date=January 30, 2020}}</ref> At the conclusion of the regular season. Cumberland was named to the First Team All-AAC.<ref>{{cite web |title=American Athletic Conference Announces All-Conference, All-Freshman Teams |url=https://theamerican.org/news/2020/3/9/mens-basketball-american-athletic-conference-announces-all-conference-all-freshman-teams.aspx |website=[[American Athletic Conference]] |access-date=March 11, 2020 |date=March 10, 2020}}</ref> Cumberland averaged 15.5 points and 4.9 assists per game as a senior. He finished his career seventh in school history in both points (1,782) and assists (415).<ref>{{cite news |title=Cumberland earns 1st team All-AAC honor |url=https://www.timesgazette.com/sports/46643/cumberland-earns-1st-team-all-aac-honor |access-date=April 8, 2020 |work=[[The Times-Gazette]] |date=March 11, 2020}}</ref>

==Professional career==
Cumberland was selected 12th overall in the 2021 [[NBA G League]] draft by the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://gleague.nba.com/nba-g-league-2020-21-draft-order/|title=NBA G League 2020-21 Draft Results - NBA G League|newspaper=Nba G League}}</ref> He made his debut in their season opener on February 10, 2021.

On February 26, 2021, Cumberland was traded to the [[Raptors 905]] in exchange for center [[Dewan Hernandez]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Jarron Cumberland traded to Raptors 905 |url=https://highlandcountypress.com/Content/Sports/Sports/Article/Jarron-Cumberland-traded-to-Raptors-905/3/21/65896 |access-date=December 25, 2021 |work=Highland County Press |date=February 26, 2021 |archive-date=December 25, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211225190315/https://highlandcountypress.com/Content/Sports/Sports/Article/Jarron-Cumberland-traded-to-Raptors-905/3/21/65896 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On October 2, 2021, Cumberland was traded to the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Jarron Cumberland: Acquired by Blue Coats |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jarron-cumberland-acquired-by-blue-coats/ |access-date=December 25, 2021 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=October 2, 2021}}</ref> He was named MVP of the G League Winter Showcase, after posting 24 points, eight rebounds and six assists in the 104–98 championship game victory against the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Cumberland named MVP of G League Showcase event |url=https://www.wnewsj.com/sports/188608/cumberland-named-mvp-of-g-league-showcase-event |access-date=December 25, 2021 |work=[[News Journal (Ohio)|Wilmington News Journal]] |date=December 23, 2021}}</ref>

On December 25, 2021, Cumberland signed a 10-day contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Brener |first1=Jeremy |title=Blazers Sign Three Players to 10-Day Contracts |url=https://www.blazersedge.com/2021/12/25/22853639/portland-trail-blazers-covid-protocols-nba-basketball-christmas-day-damian-lillard-robert-covington |website=Blazers Edge |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |access-date=December 25, 2021 |date=December 25, 2021}}</ref> Cumberland appeared in three games, scoring two points and collecting three rebounds during his stint. On January 5, 2022, following the expiration of his 10-day deal, Cumberland was reacquired by the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2021-22 NBA G League transactions|date=January 5, 2022|access-date=January 5, 2022}}</ref>

On April 25, 2023, Cumberland signed with the [[Caballeros de Culiacán]] of the [[Circuito de Baloncesto de la Costa del Pacífico]], making his debut that night.<ref>{{cite web|title=Caballeros de Culiacán arranca serie en Jalisco con derrota ante Astros|url=https://www.noroeste.com.mx/deportes/mas-deportes/caballeros-de-culiacan-arranca-serie-en-jalisco-con-derrota-ante-astros-FH3768340|website=Noroeste.com.mx|date=April 25, 2023|access-date=April 26, 2023|language=Spanish}}</ref>

On October 29, 2023, Cumberland re-joined the [[Delaware Blue Coats]],<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Delaware Blue Coats|title=time for camp.🏕️ #GetYourCoatsOn|number=1718729617358418138|user=blue_coats|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=November 10, 2023}}</ref> but was waived on December 9.<ref name="Del2023-24">{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Delaware Blue Coats Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Delaware-Blue-Coats/57/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 16, 2023}}</ref> Six days later, he was reacquired by the Blue Coats.<ref name="Del2023-24" />

On September 5, 2024, Cumberland signed with [[Petro de Luanda (basketball)|Petro de Luanda]] of the [[Angolan Basketball League|Unitel Basket]].<ref>{{cite web|title=BEM-VINDO Jarron Cumberland|url=https://petroatletico.co.ao/noticia/111358|website=PetroAtletico.co.ao|date=September 5, 2024|access-date=September 28, 2024|language=Portuguese}}</ref>

On October 28, 2024, Cumberland rejoined the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Delaware Blue Coats|title=ready for camp.🫡 #GetYourCoatsOn|number=1850954040386986467|user=blue_coats|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 3, 2024}}</ref>

For the 2025–26 season, Cumberland joined the [[South Bay Lakers]] of the G League.<ref>{{cite news|title= South Bay Lakers Announce Training Camp Roster |url= https://southbay.gleague.nba.com/news/south-bay-lakers-announce-training-camp-roster |access-date=November 2, 2025 |work=[[NBA G League]] |date=October 29, 2025}}</ref> On December 24, he moved to the [[Osceola Magic]] in a three-team trade. Cumberland played 12 games for South Bay, averaging 4.5 points and 4 assists per game.<ref>{{cite news|title= OSCEOLA MAGIC ACQUIRE JARRON CUMBERLAND FROM SOUTH BAY LAKERS IN THREE-TEAM DEAL |url= https://osceola.gleague.nba.com/news/osceola-magic-acquire-jarron-cumberland-from-south-bay-lakers-in-three-team-deal |access-date=January 25, 2026 |work=[[NBA G League]] |date=December 26, 2025}}</ref>
